answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may earn from a task, then slash that stake when independent auditors prove duplicate identities coordinated to claim the same reward. A grove of honest agents can compare signed task histories, while an oasis of fresh accounts gains no advantage: each identity needs its own locked stake and time to build a record. The attacker pays real capital per sybil and risks losing it, making mass identity creation costly rather than free, even if the comet of new accounts arrives at once.
